featured_reviews.name: velita athayde
featured_reviews.review_text:
My uncle, Francis Dsouza, passed away just 16 days after being admitted to your home. This raises serious questions that the family deserves answers to.

How did his condition deteriorate to such an extent within such a short period? If he was struggling to adjust to the environment, why was the family not informed immediately?

Is it not the responsibility of the home to closely monitor new admissions, particularly during the initial adjustment period, and communicate any concerns to the family? Had we been informed of any difficulties, we could have taken appropriate action.

It is deeply concerning that there appears to have been no timely intervention or notification. A facility entrusted with the care of vulnerable individuals should have clear protocols in place to assess whether residents are adapting well to their surroundings.

There should be a policy that permits long-term stay only when a resident is demonstrably adjusting to the environment and their well-being is being maintained. The lack of communication and apparent failure to identify or address these issues has left our family shocked, disappointed, and seeking accountability.

featured_reviews.review_text: Harshamrut Foundation is truly one of the best old age homes in the Vasai-Virar region. featured_reviews.name: Maithilee Warang
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ashram is really good I kept my nani, and I must say it is a very peaceful and caring place for elderly people. The environment is calm, clean, and well-maintained, which makes the residents feel comfortable and safe.

The food provided at the ashram is very good and healthy. Meals are served on time and are freshly prepared, keeping in mind the health and dietary needs of the elderly. The staff members are kind, patient, and always ready to help the residents with anything they need.

The care given to everyone here is truly heart-warming. The staff regularly checks on the residents and makes sure they are comfortable, happy, and healthy. They treat everyone with respect and affection, almost like family.

One of the best things about this ashram is the positive and friendly atmosphere. The residents spend time together talking, sharing stories, and supporting each other. They often play devotional songs and music, which creates a peaceful and spiritual environment. Sometimes they also sing together, celebrate small festivals, and enjoy group activities that keep everyone engaged.

The place is very clean and organized, with proper rooms, good ventilation, and peaceful surroundings. It truly feels like a home rather than just an institution. When we kept our nani her weight was very low she wasn't healthy but because of ashram she became very healthy and strong

Overall, this ashram is a wonderful place for elderly people to stay. It provides good food, proper care, companionship, and a peaceful lifestyle. I feel happy knowing that my nani is in such a loving and supportive environment.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Great place. We can't ask for more.
Separate floors for mein women.
Very well ventilated halls.
An open front yard for sunbathing or any other activity.
TV for entertainment
Food although I haven't eaten there but my father who lived there for a month shared his experience., is very good.
Assistance by the helps there is 24 x 7.
Medicines are taken care of by timings.
I do recommend this place for a short stay definitely but probably must be good for a long term too
